3. The contrary case of the defendant is such that the claim of the plaintiff is false and baseless and the suit is hit by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquisance. There was no talk of sale between the plaintiff and defendant no.1 and there was no fixation of consideration amount Take 1,10,000/-(Take One lac and ten thousand) in respect of the suit land measuring 1.20 acres of land. The defendant no.1 did not obtain Taka 30,000/- (Take Thirty thousand) from the plaintiff and not executed the bainanama in favour of the plaintiff and the plaintiff did not send the amount of Taka 60,000/-(Taka sixty thousand) which was received by the defendant rather the plaintiff behind the back of the defendant no.1 on 04.01.1997 sent an amount of Taka 60,000/- in the Savings Bank's account of the defendant no.1 and the defendant no.1 returned that amount on 25.01.1997. The further case of the defendant no.2 is such that he purchased the land from the defendant no.1 within the knowledge of the plaintiff and the kabla deed in favour of the defendant no.2 is genuine and not collusive or forged. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-appellant-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay of Other Execution case no. 05 of 2005 pending in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 30 Court, Mymensingh. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 

 10. On perusal of the case record it transpires that admittedly the disputed land comprising an area of 1.20 acres of land originally belonged to the defendant no.1 of the original suit Abdul Razzak, who is the uncle of the plaintiff. It is the case of the plaintiff that his uncle for want of money for the purpose of pilgrimage proposed to sale the land and the plaintiff agreed to purchase. The consideration amount was fixed Tk. 1,10,000/-(Taka One lac and its thousand) and out of that amount Tk. 30,000/- (Take Thirty thousand) was paid in advance in favour of the vendor of the deed i.e. the original owner defendant no.1 and the further case of the plaintiff is such that the defendant no.1 after taking the advance money executed a bainapatra i.e. a deed of agreement in favour of plaintiff on 10.12.1996 A.D. and it was settled within the contract of that bainapatra marked Exhibit-1 that the remaining amount of the consideration money would have to be paid by the plaintiff within last part of January 1997 and if it is paid the defendant no.1 would execute and register a Sub-kabla deed in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff thereafter pursuant to the aforesaid condition of the deed of agreement on 04.01.1997 sent Tk.60,000/-through Sonali Bank, Munshiganj Branch from his place of work in favour of his uncle vide M.T. dated 04.01.1997. It was decided between the parties that after taking the remaining balance amount of Taka 20,000/- the defendant No.1 will execute and register the kabla deed, but the defendant not can of ill motive on 19.01.1997 knowing the previous talk of sale and execution of the deed of agreement managed to get a kabla deed registered from Iswarganj Sub-registry office, Mymensingh from the defendant no.1. 

 11. The said contention of the plaintiff-opposite party has been controverted from the side of the defendant-petitioners and the defendant petitioners by filing separate written statement denied the case of the plaintiff-opposite party and also denied the execution of deed of agreement with the plaintiff-opposite party in respect of the suit land at a consideration of Tk. 1,10,000/-(Take One lac and ten thousand) and also denied the execution of the deed of agreement. To substantiate the respective claim and counter claim of the parties to the suit the plaintiff adduced seven witnesses and the defendant adduced three witnesses. 

 13. Having gone through the materials and evidence on record, I find that the plaintiff to the suit is a service holder, who is the witness no.1 Md. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan. This witness was examined by the trial court and the, plaintiff during his examination supported his plaint. The witness no. 2 for the plaintiff is one Sajimuddin, who corroborated the plaintiff in respect of the specific case of the plaintiff upon the deed of agreement between the plaintiff and defendant no. 1. In his presence out of the total consideration amount, Taka 30,000/- was paid in advance and the bainanama was executed in which this witness put his signature. He identified his signature marked as Exhibit-1(b). The witness no.3 Wahed Ali was also present at the time of deed of agreement as witness lie put his signature which has been marked as Exhibit-1(c) after his identification. The witness no.4 Abdur Rashid is another witness of the deed of agreement. This witness claimed himself a presentee at the time of payment of money. He states at a stage that the plaintiff paid Taka 30,000/- to the defendant no.1 out of the total consideration amount in his presence. The witness no.5 Abdul laid is a hearsay witness of the case. The witness no.6 Khowaj Ali a Union Parishad Chairman of the concern Union Perished No. 6 Mahishbag, P.S. Ishwatganj, District-Mymensingh deposed in favour of the plaintiff's case and states that the disputed land is situated within Mouza Daogram and the defendant No.1for the purpose of performing holy pilgrimage for want of money proposed to sale the property. There was an agreement for sale between the plaintiff and defendant no.1 those who are known to him (U.P. Chairman Md. Khowaj Ali). This witness further states that he told the defendant no. 2 that the plaintiff entered into an agreement with the defendant No.1 in inspect of the suit land and the defendant not as such was in the know about the deed of agreement from its very beginning. The last witness Ibrahim Sarkar is a deed writer, who wrote the bainanama dated 14.12.1996. Vis-a-vis; the witness no.1 for the defendants Md. Abdur Razzak was the admitted owner of the suit land & he is the defendant No.1. This witness tried to corroborate his written statement in his deposition but during his cross-examination he states at a stage, (quote) “মামলার জমি বাদী ও ২নং বিবাদীকে খরিদ করার জন্য পি,ডব্লিউ-৬ বলেছিল। অমিয় বাবু রাজি না হওয়ায় বাদীকে জমি বিক্রয় করি।” The witness no.2 for the defendant-petitioners is the defendant no.2 Amiya Kumar Maitre who is the petitioner no.1 of this present revisional application. This witness in his testimony alleges that there was no agreement between the plaintiff and defendant no.1 rather the suit land was sold by the defendant no. 1 in his favour by a registered Sub-kabla deed dated 19, 01.1997. The witness no. 3 for the defendants Abdul Karim is a formal witness of the case, who is a bank official of Sonali Bank, lswarganj Branch. The last witness Md. Abdul Gafur for the defendant-petitioners-states about a third case that the defendant no.1 proposed the sale the suit land in his favour in the year 1996 and prior to that the defendant no.1 proposed the plaintiff to purchase the same. 

 14. On careful scrutiny over the connected papers it transpires that the court of appeal below during deciding the merit of the appeal discussed the evidence adduced during trial and it was a findings of the court of appeal that the witnesses of the plaintiff successfully proved the plaintiff's case in tote. These witnesses are competent, credible, independent and trustworthy in comparison with that of the defendant's witnesses. Scaning the whole evidence I have the reason to draw such inference that the learned Court is quite justified. Apart from this; comparing the signature of the executant of the deed with his admitted signatures within the papers/documents on record it is obvious to note that the signature is the product of same individual. Under the ambit of section 73 of the Evidence Act both the trial court as well as the appellate court compared the signature of the defendant no.1 with his admitted signatures and it is their clear observation and findings that in fact the defendant no.1 Abdur Razzak executed the deed of agreement in favour of the plaintiff. It was also held by both the courts below concurrently. after sifting of evidence properly that the owner of the land after taking a sum of Take 30,000/-. (Taka Thirty thousand) executed the deed of agreement bainapatra and it was duly effected. As regard the case and contention of the defendant no. 2 it was observed by the court of appeal below that the defendant no. 2 was in the know about the transaction and existence of "baina chukti" between the parties to the suit prior to him and knowing fully well about the deed of agreement between the plaintiff and defendant no.1 he purchased the land subsequently and hence; he is not a bonafide purchaser with value. It was further observed by the beamed court after evaluation of the evidence on record that for the purpose of sale the deed of agreement was executed between the plaintiff and the defendant no.1 and the defendant not after taking a sum of Taka 30,000/- as advance payment of the partial consideration amount executed the deed. In this context in view of the materials on Record especially after assessing the evidence; both oral and documentary led by the parties to the suit it is held that the signature as it appears in the deed of agreement (Exhibit-1) is genuine and not at all manipulated or created subsequently for the purpose of the suit rather under the purview of law it has been thoroughly compared by both the courts below and concurrently the trial court as well as the appellate court in their observation and findings opined that Exhibit-1 the deed of agreement is not a created document rather it has been duly executed by its executant the defendant no.1, who is the petitioner no.2 of this revisional application. If I consider the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties it can be apparently said that the admitted owner of the deed i.e. the defendant no.1 to the original suit who deposed as witness no.1 during trial clearly admitted the case of the plaintiff and there is no ambiguity in believing the bonafide of the plaintiff-opposite party. 

 15. I have consulted the reported case laws referred from the sides of the respective parties thoroughly and considering all these it is needless to advert that, it is a clearly decided matter that the court is quite empowered under section 73 of the Evidence Act to compare the signature and such comparison to estimate similarity, or dissimilarity is immune from any question. The concurrent findings and decisions arrived at by the trial court as well as the appellate court on proper sifting of evidence & appreciation of law deserve no interference inasmuch as there is no such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice is noticed by which it can be held that the judgments are perverse. Moreover, there lordships in a case law reported in 1 MLR(AD) 418 held, whether a bainapatra is genuine or not is a finding of fact. Law enjoins that the court of appeal is the final court of fact. 

 16. I have already discussed earlier that in the instant case we have come across that both the courts below after through discussions over the evidence on record and materials concurrently observed that there was a contract between the parties to the suit and subsequent to that contract the sale deed as it appears was executed and registered between the defendant no.1 and the defendant no.2 there is nothing to hold such a view in comparison to the facts and circumstances of the case along with the evidence that in disposing the appeal the lower appellate court failed to comply with the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and there has been any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice or that in passing the impugned judgment and decree there has been any misconception of law and that the findings of facts arrived at by the lower appellate court have been founded on misrepresentation or misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise perverse contrary to law, evidence and other material on record. Except some minor discrepancies them is nothing on record to hold such a view that there has been any miscarriage of justice or in deciding the merit of the case the learned appellate court below committed any illegality or irregularity whatsoever. 

 19. The order of stay of other Execution case No.05 of 2005 of the trial court granted earlier by this. Court at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.
